description: Run Traces page — a multi-view execution trace analysis tool showing parent-child span relationships, operation durations, phase groupings, and performance insights. Provides three visualization modes: a waterfall timeline, a flamechart showing where time is spent (with gap collapsing), and a cross-run comparison view for regression detection. All views are powered by the execution_spans API (GET /execution-spans?execution_id={id}&order=asc) which returns TraceSpan records with trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, duration_ms, and phase information. Data is polled every 2 seconds for live updates via React Query. The page is mounted inside RunSelectionProvider, which supplies the selected run ID from the RunSelector dropdown in RunPageLayout.

groups.name: View Mode Navigation
groups.description: The Traces page offers three visualization modes via tab buttons: Waterfall (default, timeline-positioned spans), Flamechart (gap-collapsed, duration-proportional), and Comparison (cross-run diff). Users switch between modes using the tab bar at the top of the widget. The active tab is visually highlighted. Each mode shares the same underlying span data from useTraceViewerData but presents it differently. The Waterfall and Flamechart views share the SpanDetailPanel sidebar and PerformanceInsights footer; the Comparison view has its own summary bar and inline detail expansion.

assertions.description: Users see three view mode tabs — Waterfall, Flamechart, and Comparison — allowing them to switch between different trace visualization approaches
Users can access the Flamechart view which shows time-proportional span widths with idle gaps collapsed
Users can access the Comparison view which diffs execution spans between two runs of the same workflow
The currently active view tab is visually distinguished from inactive tabs so users know which view they are in
assertions.expected: The active tab has a highlighted background (bg-zinc-700) while inactive tabs have no background

groups.name: Trace Waterfall Visualization
groups.description: The default view is a waterfall chart that visualizes execution spans as horizontal bars arranged on a timeline. Each bar represents an operation (workflow phase, AI session, verification step, command execution, etc.) and its width indicates duration relative to total trace time. Parent-child relationships between spans create a hierarchical tree structure via depth-based indentation. The waterfall uses react-window for virtualization (32px row height), supporting traces with hundreds of spans. Time bounds are computed from all spans (not just filtered), ensuring the timeline stays stable as filters change. The timeline header shows time marks at 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of total duration.

assertions.description: Users see a waterfall-style timeline visualization where execution spans are displayed as horizontal bars, with bar width proportional to duration and vertical position showing the span hierarchy
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow has been run and the run is selected in RunSelector

assertions.description: Users see parent-child relationships between spans via depth-based indentation (20px per level), showing how high-level operations decompose into sub-operations
assertions.precondition: A run with hierarchical spans (parent_span_id relationships) is selected

assertions.description: Each span is color-coded by its workflow phase: setup (blue), verification (amber), agentic (purple), completion (emerald), AI (green), python (orange), unknown (zinc). Phase is inferred from the span name via inferPhase()
assertions.expected: Phase badges appear next to each span name with color matching: setup=blue, verification=amber, agentic=purple, completion=emerald, ai=green, python=orange
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow has been run

assertions.description: Each span in the waterfall shows its formatted duration (ms/s/m) to the right of the timeline bar, allowing quick identification of the longest-running operations
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow has been run

groups.name: Flamechart Visualization
groups.description: The Flamechart view is a canvas-based (HTML5 Canvas) stacked visualization that shows span hierarchy by call depth, with each span's width proportional to its duration. Unlike the waterfall (which shows wall-clock position), the flamechart collapses idle gaps between sibling spans so it shows where time is *spent*. Children are packed proportionally within their parent's width range — a parent with two children of 600ms and 400ms allocates 60% and 40% of its width respectively, regardless of idle gaps between them. The canvas renders at device pixel ratio for crisp display on HiDPI screens, with a dark zinc-900 background. Phase colors use raw hex values (not Tailwind) for canvas rendering.

assertions.description: The Flamechart view renders spans as colored rectangles on an HTML5 Canvas element, with width proportional to span duration and vertical stacking by call depth (22px row height + 2px gap)
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow has been run and the Flamechart tab is selected

assertions.description: The flamechart collapses idle gaps between sibling spans, so children are packed proportionally within their parent's width. This makes the chart show where time is spent rather than when operations occurred
assertions.expected: Sibling spans with idle time between them appear adjacent in the flamechart, not separated by gaps. Each child's width fraction equals its duration / total sibling duration

assertions.description: Spans wide enough (>60px rendered width) display their name and duration as text inside the rectangle, clipped to the rectangle bounds
assertions.expected: Text labels appear inside rectangles that are wide enough, formatted as 'spanName (duration)'

assertions.description: Users can zoom the flamechart horizontally via mouse wheel (1x to 50x) and pan via click-drag. Zoom keeps the mouse position stable. A 'Reset zoom' button appears when zoomed in
assertions.expected: Mouse wheel zooms horizontally (min 1x, max 50x). Click-drag pans. 'Reset zoom' button appears when zoom > 1x
assertions.precondition: Flamechart tab is active and the view has been zoomed in

assertions.description: Users can limit the maximum visible depth via a depth slider, hiding deeply nested spans to focus on high-level structure
assertions.precondition: Flamechart tab is active

assertions.description: Users can double-click a span with children to focus on its subtree, making it the new root. A breadcrumb trail (Root / parent / child) allows navigation back to any ancestor level
assertions.expected: The breadcrumb trail always shows 'Root' at the left. After double-clicking a span, its name appears in the breadcrumb. Clicking any breadcrumb segment navigates to that level
assertions.precondition: Flamechart tab is active

assertions.description: Hovering over a span shows a tooltip with the span name, duration, percentage of total, error status, and critical path info. The tooltip follows the cursor and includes a 'Double-click to focus subtree' hint
assertions.expected: Fixed-position tooltip appears near cursor showing: span name, formatted duration, percentage of root duration, error indicator if failed, critical path status and slack if critical path is enabled
assertions.precondition: Flamechart tab is active and user is hovering over a span

groups.name: Cross-Run Trace Comparison
groups.description: The Comparison view enables side-by-side analysis of execution spans from two runs of the same workflow, highlighting timing differences, added/removed spans, and regressions. It aligns spans between runs by matching on name + phase + iteration, then classifies each pair as unchanged, faster, slower, added, removed, or status_changed. The view defaults to comparing the current run (Run B) against the most recent prior run with the same workflow_name (Run A). Both runs can be overridden via dropdown selectors. Data is fetched from the same execution_spans API for each run independently via useTraceComparisonData, which calls useTraceViewerData for each run ID.

assertions.description: Users see two run selector dropdowns — 'Run A (baseline)' and 'Run B (current)' — populated with recent task runs, allowing them to pick which runs to compare
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active and at least two runs exist

assertions.description: The baseline (Run A) auto-selects the most recent prior run with the same workflow_name as the selected run. If no matching prior run exists, baseline is null and the user sees a message to select runs
assertions.expected: Run A dropdown pre-selects the previous run with the same workflow_name. If only one run exists, no baseline is selected and an explanatory message is shown
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active

assertions.description: A summary bar at the top shows the total duration of each run, the overall percentage change, and counts of faster/slower/added/removed/status-changed spans
assertions.expected: Shows 'Run A: Xs', 'Run B: Xs', '+/-N.N% overall', and colored counts for each status category
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active with two runs selected

assertions.description: When regressions are detected (>50% slower spans, success→error status changes, or new error spans), a red banner lists them by name with percentage or failure details
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active and the compared runs contain regressions

assertions.description: Users can filter the match list by status category (All, Slower, Faster, Added, Removed, Status Changed, Unchanged) with counts shown for each category
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active with two runs selected

assertions.description: Each matched span pair is shown as a row with status badge, span name, phase, duration for Run A, duration for Run B, and the delta (absolute and percentage). Rows are sorted by severity: status_changed first, then slower, added, removed, faster, unchanged
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active with two runs selected

assertions.description: Clicking a matched span pair expands inline to show a duration comparison bar chart, status change details (if applicable), and an attribute diff showing which attributes changed between runs
assertions.expected: The expanded area shows horizontal bar charts for Run A and Run B durations, with the longer run's bar in red (if slower) or green (if faster). Attribute diffs show old→new values
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active and a match row has been clicked

assertions.description: When no baseline run is available (workflow has only been run once), users see a message explaining that at least two runs are needed for comparison
assertions.precondition: Comparison tab is active and only one run exists for the workflow

groups.name: Critical Path Analysis
groups.description: When the 'Critical Path' checkbox is enabled, the system computes and highlights the longest sequential chain of spans from root to leaf — the critical path that determines total execution time. The algorithm walks the span tree bottom-up: each node's 'weight' is its own duration plus the maximum child weight. The root-to-leaf path with the highest total weight is the critical path. For parallel siblings, only the longest is on the critical path. Non-critical spans have 'slack' — how much longer they could run without extending total time. This analysis works on both the Waterfall and Flamechart views and is computed on-demand (only when the toggle is checked) via computeCriticalPath() in trace-utils.ts.

assertions.description: Users can enable critical path highlighting via a 'Critical Path' checkbox in the toolbar, available on both Waterfall and Flamechart views (not on Comparison)
When enabled in the Waterfall view, spans on the critical path appear at full opacity with bold text and a red glow border, while non-critical spans are dimmed to 40% opacity
assertions.expected: Critical path spans: opacity 1, font-medium text, ring-1 ring-red-400/60 with box shadow. Non-critical spans: opacity 0.4
assertions.precondition: Critical Path toggle is checked and at least one run with multiple spans is selected

assertions.description: A dashed red SVG line connects consecutive critical path spans in the waterfall's timeline column, making the critical path visually traceable through the span hierarchy
assertions.expected: Dashed red lines (stroke #ef4444, strokeDasharray 4 3) connect the center of each critical path span's timeline bar to the next one
assertions.precondition: Critical Path toggle is checked and the trace has at least 2 spans on the critical path

assertions.description: When enabled in the Flamechart view, critical path spans have a red stroke border and full opacity, while non-critical spans render at 35% opacity
assertions.expected: Critical path spans: globalAlpha 1, strokeStyle #ef4444, lineWidth 1.5. Non-critical: globalAlpha 0.35
assertions.precondition: Flamechart tab is active and Critical Path toggle is checked

assertions.description: The PerformanceInsights footer shows critical path statistics: total critical path duration with percentage of overall time, the bottleneck span (longest individual span on the path), and parallel slack (time saved by parallelism)
assertions.expected: Footer shows 'Critical path: Xs (N%)' | 'Bottleneck: spanName (Xs)' | 'Parallel slack: Xs'
assertions.precondition: Critical Path toggle is checked

assertions.description: When a span is selected with critical path enabled, the SpanDetailPanel shows whether the span is on the critical path or its slack time. Critical path spans show 'On critical path'. Non-critical spans show 'Off critical path' with 'Slack: Xs'

target.label: Critical path info in detail panel

assertions.expected: For critical path spans: 'On critical path' in red text. For non-critical: 'Off critical path' with slack duration
assertions.precondition: Critical Path toggle is checked and a span is selected

groups.name: Filtering and Search
groups.description: The TraceToolbar provides four filter controls that work together to narrow the visible spans in Waterfall and Flamechart views (not shown in Comparison mode). Filters are applied client-side via filterSpans() after building and flattening the span tree. The toolbar also shows a span count indicator ('N / M spans' when filtered, 'M spans' when unfiltered). All filter state is maintained in the parent TraceViewerWidget and passed down.

assertions.description: Users can search for spans by name using a text input, filtering the view to show only spans whose names contain the search term (case-insensitive)
Users can filter spans by minimum duration (in milliseconds) to focus on slow operations and identify performance bottlenecks
Users can filter spans by workflow phase (All Phases, Setup, Verification, Agentic, Completion, AI, Python) using a dropdown selector
Users can filter spans by status (All Status, Success, Errors) to quickly isolate failed operations for investigation
The toolbar shows a span count that reflects the current filter state: 'N / M spans' when filtered, 'M spans' when showing all

groups.name: Span Detail Inspection
groups.description: When the user clicks a span in the Waterfall or Flamechart view, a 280px-wide detail panel opens on the right side showing comprehensive information about that span. The panel displays: span name (stripped of 'qontinui.' prefix), status (Success/Error), phase with colored badge, formatted duration, start and end timestamps, trace/span/parent IDs in monospace, error message (if any), and all span attributes as key-value pairs. When critical path is enabled, the panel also shows whether the span is on the critical path and its slack time. Clicking the same span again or clicking the close button deselects it.

assertions.description: Users can click any span in the Waterfall or Flamechart to select it and view its details in the side panel. Clicking the same span deselects it
assertions.precondition: Waterfall or Flamechart view is active with spans loaded

assertions.description: The detail panel shows span status, phase badge, duration, start/end timestamps, trace/span/parent IDs, and attributes
assertions.precondition: A span is selected in Waterfall or Flamechart view

assertions.description: Users can close the detail panel by clicking the close button (✕), which deselects the span and hides the panel
assertions.precondition: A span is selected and the detail panel is visible

assertions.description: The footer shows performance insights: total duration, span count, error count (if any), slowest span name and duration, and phase breakdown (top 3 phases by time)
assertions.precondition: At least one span is loaded in Waterfall or Flamechart view

groups.name: Empty, Loading, and Error States
groups.description: The Traces page handles four boundary states: (1) no run selected — shows 'Select a task run to view traces'; (2) loading — shows 'Loading trace data...' while the first fetch is in progress; (3) error — shows 'Failed to load traces: {error}' in red; (4) empty — shows 'No spans to display' when a run is selected but has zero execution spans. These early returns happen before any view rendering, so they apply regardless of the active view mode.

assertions.description: When no task run is selected, users see a clear prompt to select one
While trace data is being fetched for the first time, a loading message is shown
When trace data fails to load, an error message in red text shows the failure reason
Trace data is automatically refreshed every 2 seconds via React Query refetchInterval, enabling live monitoring of in-progress executions without manual refresh
assertions.expected: Span data updates automatically every 2 seconds. New spans from an in-progress execution appear without page reload
